title: Custom: Palindrome Checker with Chars & DoubleEndedIterator
summary: Check whether a word is an alphanumeric palindrome using Rust iterator adapters.
theory:
### Working with Strings & Iterators

In Rust, strings are UTF-8 encoded sequences of bytes. To inspect individual characters, use `.chars()`:

```rust
let chars: Vec<char> = "Rustacean".chars().collect();
```

You can also compare a forward iterator against a reverse iterator (`.rev()`):

```rust
let clean: Vec<char> = s.chars()
    .filter(|c| c.is_alphanumeric())
    .map(|c| c.to_ascii_lowercase())
    .collect();

clean.iter().eq(clean.iter().rev())
```
requirements: Filter only alphanumeric characters and treat uppercase/lowercase identically
Return true if the text reads the same backward as forward, false otherwise
hints: Clue 2: Collect the characters into a `Vec<char>`: `let chars: Vec<char> = ...collect();`.
